name: Director's Cut
focus: Org design, managing managers, headcount and budget, AI strategy, system design judgment.

cards.title: Load balancer
cards.body: Put many app servers behind one entry point. Adds a hop and needs health checks. Use when horizontal scale starts.
cards.recallPrompt: Main tradeoff of a load balancer?

cards.title: Cache vs origin
cards.body: Cache when the same data is read far more than written. You gain latency and load relief; you pay in staleness and invalidation complexity.
cards.recallPrompt: When do you reach for a cache?

cards.title: CDN
cards.body: Edge-cache static files or media for users everywhere. Tradeoffs: cost and cache purges when content changes.

cards.title: Relational database
cards.body: Use for transactions, joins, strong consistency (money, enrollment). Harder to scale writes than a simple NoSQL pattern.
cards.recallPrompt: When is SQL the right default?

cards.title: NoSQL store
cards.body: Huge scale, simple access patterns, flexible schema. Weaker consistency and no joins. Pick when access patterns are clear.

cards.title: Replication
cards.body: Read scaling and failover. Cost is replica lag — know what staleness your product can tolerate.

cards.title: Sharding
cards.body: Split data or writes when one machine is not enough. Hot shards and cross-shard queries become the new hard problems.

cards.title: Queue or stream
cards.body: Smooth spikes and decouple slow work. You accept eventual consistency, retries, and ordering questions.

cards.title: Search index
cards.body: Full text search and autocomplete. Extra system to run; index lag versus primary store.
cards.recallAnswer: Index lag; extra system to operate

cards.title: Object storage
cards.body: Files, images, model artifacts. Not for small frequent updates — use a DB for those.
cards.recallPrompt: When not to use object storage?

cards.title: Rate limiter
cards.body: Protect services and fair use. Legitimate users can get blocked — tune carefully and explain the policy.

cards.title: Vector database
cards.body: Semantic search for RAG and AI features. Trade recall versus latency and embedding cost.
cards.recallAnswer: Recall vs latency and embedding cost

cards.title: Step 1 — Clarify
cards.body: Who are the users, what is the core job, what is out of scope. Restate before designing.
cards.recallAnswer: Clarify users, job, out of scope

cards.title: Step 2 — Requirements
cards.body: Three to five functional requirements. Then non-functional: latency, availability, consistency, privacy, cost.

cards.title: Step 3 — Estimate
cards.body: Start from DAU. Derive reads vs writes per second and storage per year. Do the ballpark yourself — asking for every number reads badly.

cards.title: Step 4 — API and data
cards.body: Few key endpoints, main entities, SQL vs NoSQL with a reason.
cards.recallAnswer: Endpoints, entities, store choice with reason

cards.title: Step 5 — High level design
cards.body: Client, gateway, services, data stores, cache, queue. Keep it to boxes you can defend. Fewer boxes, clearly reasoned, beats many boxes.

cards.title: Step 6 — Deep dive
cards.body: Pick the hardest part (hot partitions, fan-out, contention, consistency). Show two options and why you pick one.
cards.recallPrompt: What makes a strong deep dive?
cards.recallAnswer: Two options and a reasoned pick

cards.title: Step 7 — Operate it
cards.body: Monitoring, failure modes, graceful degradation, security, cost, rollout plan.

cards.title: Step 8 — Director layer
cards.body: How you would staff it, build vs buy, phasing into milestones, biggest risks. This is where you stand out from senior engineers.

cards.title: 60-minute clock
cards.body: 0–5 frame · 5–15 requirements and scale · 15–30 HLD · 30–45 deep dive · 45–55 changed requirement · 55–60 your questions.
cards.recallAnswer: Adapt calmly to a changed requirement

cards.title: Scenario answer shape
cards.body: Context → Decision → Tradeoff → Action through others → Result with a number → Reflection. Keep under two minutes.
cards.recallPrompt: Six parts of a scenario answer?
cards.recallAnswer: Context, decision, tradeoff, action, result, reflection

cards.title: AI lens — Outcome
cards.body: Which business metric moves: revenue, retention, cost to serve, time saved.

cards.title: AI lens — Use case portfolio
cards.body: Rank ideas by value and feasibility. Start with one wedge that ships in a quarter.
cards.recallPrompt: How do you pick the first AI wedge?
cards.recallAnswer: Value × feasibility; ships in a quarter

cards.title: AI lens — Build, buy, or partner
cards.body: Frontier API, open weights, fine-tuned small model, or vendor. Decide on cost, control, latency, privacy.

cards.title: AI lens — Platform vs product
cards.body: Shared platform (evals, guardrails, model gateway, agent identity) versus embedded teams shipping features.
cards.recallPrompt: What belongs on a shared AI platform?

cards.title: AI lens — Quality and evaluation
cards.body: Offline evals, human review, online metrics, regression gates before release.

cards.title: AI lens — Cost
cards.body: Token and inference cost per task, caching, smaller models where good enough.
cards.recallPrompt: How do you control AI cost?
cards.recallAnswer: Cost per task, caching, smaller models

cards.title: AI lens — Risk and governance
cards.body: Privacy, hallucination in high-risk flows, audit trails, human in the loop, regulation.
cards.recallAnswer: Human in the loop and audit trails

cards.title: AI lens — Org and talent
cards.body: Who to hire first, how to upskill existing engineers, how teams are structured.

cards.title: AI lens — Adoption
cards.body: Change management, trust, measuring real usage rather than demos.
cards.recallPrompt: How do you know AI landed?

cards.title: URL shortener
cards.body: Design a URL shortener on the 60-minute clock. Cover uniqueness, redirects, analytics, and abuse.
cards.recallPrompt: Name one hard part of a URL shortener.
cards.recallAnswer: Unique ID generation at scale / hot keys

cards.title: Notification system
cards.body: Push, email, SMS with preferences, fan-out, and delivery guarantees.

cards.title: News feed
cards.body: Push vs pull fan-out, ranking, and celebrity problem.
cards.recallAnswer: Hybrid fan-out / pull for huge followings

cards.title: Chat and messaging
cards.body: Presence, delivery receipts, ordering, offline sync, media.
cards.recallPrompt: How do you handle offline messages?

cards.title: Rate limiter
cards.body: Token bucket vs sliding window; distributed counters; user vs IP keys.

cards.title: File storage like Dropbox
cards.body: Chunking, dedupe, sync conflict resolution, metadata vs blob store.

cards.title: Search autocomplete
cards.body: Trie / prefix index, personalization, latency budget under 100ms.

cards.title: Payments ledger
cards.body: Strong consistency, idempotency, double-entry, reconciliation.

cards.title: Course registration at peak
cards.body: Home turf: 40,000 students hit enroll at 7am. Contention, fairness, queues. Director layer: staffing and SLOs.

cards.title: AI advisor degree plan
cards.body: RAG over student records with privacy, evaluation, and cost controls.
cards.recallAnswer: Student privacy and wrong advice risk

cards.title: Safe agent platform
cards.body: Many agents act on student records: permissions, audit, rollback.

cards.title: LLM query batching
cards.body: Real Anthropic-style prompt: design end-to-end batching for LLM queries.

cards.title: Claims agent with RAG
cards.body: Scale AI style: claims agent using RAG while controlling token cost.

cards.title: Confident wrong answers
cards.body: Mitigate a model giving confident but wrong answers in high-risk contexts.

cards.title: Org design
cards.body: Your org chart is broken. How do you fix it? Name the managers you would put in place.
cards.recallPrompt: What must a director answer name?
cards.recallAnswer: The managers and roles to put in place

cards.title: Managing managers
cards.body: Tell me about developing a manager. Action through others; result with a number.

cards.title: Underperformance
cards.body: A manager on your team is struggling. Decision, tradeoff, and what you did through leaders.

cards.title: Cross-team conflict
cards.body: Two teams disagree on a design. How did you turn disagreement into a decision people stand behind?

cards.title: Prioritization
cards.body: How do you say no to a senior stakeholder?

cards.title: Failure or incident
cards.body: Your biggest miss and what changed after. Reflection is required.

cards.title: Hiring bar
cards.body: How do you set and hold the hiring bar across managers?
cards.recallAnswer: Bar across managers, not one team

cards.title: Budget and headcount
cards.body: Annualize a headcount plan; price a shared deadline.
cards.recallPrompt: Who is often in the room?

cards.title: Ambiguity
cards.body: Building a team from zero (the ML mission team). Vision plus first hires.
cards.recallAnswer: First hires and a wedge outcome

cards.title: AI adoption
cards.body: Getting teams to actually use AI — usage over demos.

cards.title: Influence
cards.body: Driving change without authority.

cards.title: Vision
cards.body: Where would you take this org in two years?

cards.title: Annualize headcount
cards.body: Take a hiring plan by month and annualize fully loaded cost. Be ready to explain assumptions to finance.
cards.recallAnswer: Full-year cost of the hire plan

cards.title: Price a shared deadline
cards.body: Given a date, price overtime, contractors, scope cuts, and risk. Speak in dollars and delivery confidence.

cards.title: Fix a broken org chart
cards.body: Name managers and spans. Separate platform vs product. Show who owns outcomes.
cards.recallPrompt: What separates director from manager loops?

cards.title: Director loop shape
cards.body: Usually 4–6 stages over 2–8 weeks: recruiter → hiring manager → system design → panels/exhibit → final. Nobody asks a director to whiteboard code.
cards.recallAnswer: Tech, business strategy, and people leadership meeting

cards.title: Consistency across rounds
cards.body: Only ~20% of candidates perform consistently. Even strong candidates bomb roughly one session in five. Mock practice is required.
cards.recallAnswer: Loops reward repetition; variance is high

quizzes.prompt: What do interviewers score most in a director system design round?
quizzes.explanation: Architecture is the medium; judgment is what gets scored.

quizzes.prompt: Read-heavy profile with acceptable staleness. Best first building block?
quizzes.explanation: Cache when reads dwarf writes and staleness is OK.

quizzes.prompt: Put the first four system design steps in order.
quizzes.explanation: Clarify → Requirements → Estimate → API/data before HLD.
choices: Clarify → Requirements → Estimate → API and data
Estimate → Clarify → High level design → Requirements
API and data → Clarify → Estimate → Requirements

quizzes.prompt: 40k students hit enroll in 10 minutes. Approx enroll attempts per second?
A strong director scenario answer must include:
quizzes.explanation: Result with a number: delivery, retention, cost, quality, or adoption.

quizzes.prompt: First move on AI strategy for a product?
choices: Pick the metric that should move
quizzes.explanation: Outcome lens first: which business metric moves.

quizzes.prompt: Which question separates director loops from manager loops?
quizzes.explanation: Money, structure, and leaders of leaders.

quizzes.prompt: Agents acting on student records. Highest priority control?
Minutes 30–45 on the clock are for:

quizzes.explanation: Context → Decision → Tradeoff → Action → Result → Reflection.
choices: Context → Decision → Tradeoff → Action → Result → Reflection
Result → Context → Action → Decision → Tradeoff → Reflection
Decision → Action → Context → Result → Tradeoff → Reflection
Context → Action → Result → Decision → Tradeoff → Reflection
